Archie Mobile · In build

Your computer, from your pocket.

Archie Mobile is the app we are building for your phone. It reaches the agent on your computer from wherever you are.

iPhoneApp Store Not there yet
AndroidGoogle Play After the iPhone app

The conversation

The app reaches your agent. It does not run it.

Nothing about your agent moves to your phone. It stays on the computer you installed it on, with your files, your passwords and your connected accounts, and it runs there whether your phone is in your hand, in your pocket, or flat. The app is a way to reach that computer and tell it things.

So the app works while that computer is awake and online, the same as your chat app does today.

Most of the desk

Most of what you do at the computer, from here.

Start an agent or stop it, add an add-on or take one off, finish an add-on’s setup, turn a routine on and off or move the time it runs, rename it, change its face, read what it has been doing, and talk to it.

What it cannot reach is what never leaves your computer: your passwords and keys, your knowledge files, and the rows inside a collection.

Sealed

Sealed before the message leaves your computer.

Right now your agent reaches you through a chat app, so what it says to you crosses that company’s servers like any other message you send there. This app will not work that way. Your computer seals every message before it leaves, with a key it makes itself and gives to your phone by showing it a code to scan. The key never passes through us. We hold the sealed messages and cannot open them.

  • We still see when a message was left, which version of Archie wrote it, and whether it is waiting, done or failed. Never what it said.
  • Whoever holds the phone holds the key. Unpair it on the computer and that key retires.
  • Your chat app keeps working. This is a second door, not a replacement.

Side by side

Who can open what.

Each company’s own published words, and the app we are building on the last row.

Each chat app Archie connects to, what that company publishes about encryption, and whether that company can open your agent’s messages, compared with the app Otian is building.
  What that company publishes Can that company read it
Telegram An ordinary chat, which is the kind an agent uses, is not end to end. Telegram’s FAQ says cloud chats are “stored encrypted in the Telegram Cloud”, and that “several court orders from different jurisdictions are required to force us to give up any data”. Its end-to-end kind, a Secret Chat, is between two people and is not something an agent can useSource 1 Yes
Discord Every voice and video call is end-to-end encrypted. Text is not, in Discord’s own words: “We have no current plans to extend E2EE to text messages”Source 2 Yes
Slack “In Slack, customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default.” Archie joins as an ordinary bot, so your agent’s messages sit in that workspace like every other message in itSource 3 Yes
Matrix A Matrix room can be end-to-end encrypted. Archie cannot read one that is, so our connect guide asks for a room with encryption off. The same trade as the others, and it is our limitation rather than Matrix’sSource 4 Yes
iMessage on a Mac The exception. Apple encrypts it end to end and says “no one else can access your end-to-end encrypted data, not even Apple”. Archie reads it out of the Messages app on your own computer rather than over the networkSource 5 No
The app we are building Sealed on your computer before it leaves, under a key it gives your phone by camera. We hold the sealed messages and have no keySource 6 No, and neither can we
On your phone

Three things the app asks your phone for.

Each is asked for at the moment it is needed. The App Store makes us write down why, so here it is.

The camera

For two things. It reads the square code that pairs the phone with your computer, and it takes a photo when you choose to show one to an agent. It is not on at any other time.

Your photos

Only at the moment you pick one to send. The app is handed the picture you chose and nothing else, and it never reads the rest of your library.

The microphone

Only while you are recording something to say to an agent. You start that by pressing the talk button, you can throw the recording away instead of sending it, and it stops on its own if you leave the app.

A photo or a voice note goes to the computer running Archie, sealed, and we cannot read it.

Where Archie Mobile stands

Written and running. In neither store.

The iPhone app is written and runs on our own phones. It is not in the App Store, Android comes after it, and we cannot give you a date and will not invent one. Nothing about your setup has to change to be ready for it.

Sources for every claim on this page
1Telegram, on cloud chats and Secret Chats

“Secret chats use end-to-end encryption” while “Cloud Chats use client-server/server-client encryption and are stored encrypted in the Telegram Cloud”, and “several court orders from different jurisdictions are required to force us to give up any data”. From the Telegram FAQ, read on September 11, 2026.

2Discord, on what its encryption covers

Discord’s DAVE protocol covers “every voice and video call on Discord, whether in DMs, group DMs, voice channels, or Go Live streams”, and on text: “We have no current plans to extend E2EE to text messages.” From Discord’s own announcement, read on September 11, 2026.

3Slack, on encryption

“In Slack, customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default.” From Slack’s security page, read on September 11, 2026.

4Matrix, and our own limitation

This row is about Archie, not about Matrix. Our connection cannot read an encrypted room, so the connect guide asks for one with encryption off. Matrix supports end-to-end encryption well; the shortfall is ours.

5Apple, on iMessage

“No one else can access your end-to-end encrypted data, not even Apple.” From Apple’s iCloud data security overview, read on September 11, 2026. One caveat Apple states on the same page and we will not leave out: Messages in iCloud is end-to-end encrypted when iCloud Backup is off, so if you keep iCloud Backup on, check how Apple describes that before relying on it.

6Our side of the table

The sealed mailbox already exists and already carries phone access: what we hold and what we cannot open is on the Trust page, each line pointing at the code behind it. Messages are sealed with AES-256-GCM, an ordinary published cipher rather than anything of our own invention, and the key travels in the part of a web address browsers never send to a server. Both of those you can run rather than take from us: seal a message of your own and try to open it without the key.

What we have not claimed

Nothing here says Telegram, Discord or Slack read your messages. It says what each publishes about what it can do, and links their words so you can check ours. Nothing here says a chat app is unsafe: your agent works there today and we built those connections on purpose. And nothing claims to be the most secure anything: we have described one mechanism and shown you where it fails.

Reaching your agent already works.

Connecting a chat app takes a few minutes and is the last step of setting an agent up. The app is a second door. The first one is open now.
